Its main features are per-learner structured namespaces, pre-retrieval policy-enforced access control, a strict counselling isolation wall, PDPA-oriented audit of every operation, an async write path and cached read path, and an out-of-band Memory Management Plane for configuration and governance. The document is written to be detailed enough for an engineering team or AI coding assistant to start building, and Section 28 assesses where that is not yet true. content.text: {"answers":[{"question_id":"RQ-002","status":"answered","summary":"With an approximate pgvector HNSW index, PostgreSQL can collect candidates by vector distance first and then apply the WHERE clause. A selective filter can then return fewer rows than requested, or none (EV-027, read in full; EV-004). The design's filter is very selective: about 600 of 9.5M rows per learner. pgvector 0.8.0 added hnsw.iterative_scan, which is off by default; the design work came from issue #678 (EV-002). Other mitigations are a B-tree-first or exact scan on (learner_id, slot_path), partial indexes, or partitioning. With only 500-800 rows per learner, an exact scan after the B-tree filter is likely enough. This needs EXPLAIN ANALYZE and a benchmark to confirm. The design does not specify any of these, so the 'effective search space per query is 500-800 vectors' claim is not guaranteed by the index as written.","evidence_ids":["EV-027","EV-004","EV-002"]},{"question_id":"RQ-005","status":"partial","summary":"Official Microsoft pages on configurable token lifetimes were found (EV-006, EV-007, EV-009), but only snippets were captured. The specific limits could not be read from them: the access-token default and maximum, and how long refresh tokens and sessions last. My general knowledge is that Entra access tokens default to about 60-90 minutes, can be configured up to 1 day, and are kept alive by refresh tokens. If that holds, a 48-hour 'access token' is not configurable, and the design mixes up access-token lifetime with refresh-token or session lifetime. This is unverified until the pages are read.","evidence_ids":["EV-006","EV-007","EV-009"]},{"question_id":"RQ-006","status":"partial","summary":"Official Azure pages confirm that pgvector is a supported extension on Azure Database for PostgreSQL flexible server (EV-017, EV-018, EV-020). The installed version, and so whether iterative scan (needs 0.8.0 or later) is available, was not established from the snippets. No pricing source was retrieved for the Memory Optimised 16 vCore SKU in Southeast Asia with HA, storage and backup, so the SGD 800-1,200/month figure is unverified.","evidence_ids":["EV-017","EV-018","EV-020"]},{"question_id":"RQ-007","status":"partial","summary":"PDPA s.25 requires an organisation to stop keeping documents that contain personal data, or to anonymise them, once it is reasonable to assume the purpose is no longer served by keeping them (EV-030, primary statute, snippet only; EV-028, EV-029). Two parts of the design are in tension with this. First, agent per-learner backups that survive learner self-deletion. Second, append-only audit logs that hold personal identifiers with no defined retention period. Whether this is an actual breach depends on the documented purposes, retention periods and any legal-requirement exceptions; a DPO needs to assess that. The access/correction and consent-withdrawal provisions were not researched.","evidence_ids":["EV-030","EV-028","EV-029"]},{"question_id":"RQ-009","status":"partial","summary":"Official Azure OpenAI quota pages exist (EV-022, EV-023), but the snippets did not give the text-embedding-3-small tokens-per-minute figures.
